rows.text: Vaccines work by teaching your immune system how to recognize and fight off specific pathogens, like viruses or bacteria, without causing the disease itself. They contain harmless pieces of the pathogen (like proteins or weakened forms) that trigger an immune response, creating memory cells. If you encounter the real pathogen later, your body can quickly respond and prevent illness.
